newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Merck 96 profits surge, shares rise.
newsitem.headline: German Merck 96 profits surge, shares rise.

text.p: Shares in German pharmaceuticals company Merck KGaA were lifted on Tuesday after the company reported that its 1996 profits surged 36 percent and said the current business year had started well.
Describing 1996 as "an extremely successful year", Merck posted net profit of 502 million marks for 1996 amid a 10.9 percent rise in sales to 6.95 billion marks.
The news pushed its shares up 2.20 marks to 68 marks in early bourse trade, outperforming the broader market, where average gains were below 0.5 percent.
Merck said its pure pharmaceutical business had fuelled the advance. The division's sales rose 16 percent to 3.9 billion marks, accounting for 56 percent of group business.

Laboratory sales rose 6.3 percent to 1.7 billion marks while speciality chemicals sales advanced 5.1 percent to 1.3 billion marks. The company also said it had spent 1.2 billion marks on acquisitions.
Merck added that business had gone well in early 1997 and said sales had risen 15.9 percent in the first two months, despite a slight decline in domestic sales.
The company is to pay a 1.25 mark dividend for 1996. In 1995, Merck paid a dividend of 32 pfennigs for share for the final quarter only.
